thread.title: AI and Data Science on Databricks

chapters.title: Data storage and movement
intro: The platform starts with storage.
Data is stored once in open tables, brought in by pipelines and maintained automatically.
Transactional and real-time data sit on the same storage.

points.title: Table formats
points.effect: Keep one consistent copy of your data, in an open format.
points.challenge: Batch and streaming data often sit in separate stores, sometimes in closed or complex formats. A job that fails halfway can leave a table inconsistent. A schema change can break the jobs that read it.
points.pivot: **Delta Lake** is now the single format for batch and streaming alike.
bullets: Databricks stores the data once, in **open tables** in your cloud storage.
Delta adds **transactions** to those files.
Batch jobs and streaming jobs write to the same tables without corrupting them.
The schema can change without breaking readers.
Tables can also use **Apache Iceberg**, the other open table format.
**Multi-table transactions** commit changes to several tables at once.

pivot.text: Delta Lake provides open ACID transactions for both batch and streaming data workloads.

points.title: Ingestion and pipelines
points.effect: Connectors and pipelines are managed by the platform.
points.lead: The data then has to get into this storage.
points.challenge: Getting it there means writing connector code for each source and wiring job dependencies by hand.
points.pivot: **Lakeflow** now hands both jobs over to the platform.
bullets: It brings the data in and transforms it.
Lakeflow Connect provides **managed connectors** to databases and SaaS applications, query-based and community connectors, and Auto Loader for files.
Zerobus Ingest brings in **event data**.
**Spark Declarative Pipelines** describe the transformations, and Lakeflow works out the order in which to run them.
They are written in the Lakeflow Pipelines Editor, or on a **visual canvas** in Lakeflow Designer, and can run in **real-time mode**.
Lakeflow Jobs **orchestrates** the workflows.

pivot.text: Lakeflow provides data ingestion, orchestration, and transformation components for building data pipelines.

points.title: Transactional and real-time data
points.effect: Applications and agents keep their data on the same platform as the analytics, under the same governance.
points.lead: The analytical data is now in place. Applications and agents also read and write transactional data, and that data usually lives in a separate database with its own copy.
points.challenge: It is not governed there. Feeding analytics from it takes replication pipelines and a second system to maintain. The copies lag behind the source.
points.pivot: **Lakebase** now keeps that data next to the analytics, under the same rules.
bullets: It is a **serverless Postgres** database inside the platform, for the state of applications and agents.
**Synced tables** bring lakehouse data into Lakebase, and **Lakehouse Sync** writes Lakebase tables back to the lakehouse.
**Lakehouse//RT** answers SQL queries in **under 100 milliseconds** directly on lakehouse tables, so dashboards and applications no longer need a separate serving copy.
LTAP is the architecture these capabilities deliver: one dataset, written in Lakebase and read in Lakehouse//RT, with **no replication pipeline** between them.

effect.text: Lakebase provides serverless PostgreSQL storage for agent state and application data with Unity Catalog integration.

challenge.text: **Replication pipelines** needed between operational DB and warehouse
**Eventual consistency** lag between operational and analytical
Copied serving data **stale** vs operational source

pivot.text: Lakebase provides serverless PostgreSQL storage for agent state and application data with Unity Catalog integration.
**UC-synced** tables

points.title: Table maintenance
points.effect: Tables are maintained automatically, with no jobs to schedule.
points.lead: The tables then need maintenance.
points.challenge: Someone has to schedule it and tune it by hand.
points.pivot: **Predictive Optimization** now maintains the tables on its own.
bullets: It decides when to compact files, remove old versions and cluster the data, based on how it is queried.
It runs on **serverless compute**, and each decision is recorded for audit.

pivot.text: Predictive Optimization automatically tunes Delta tables on Unity Catalog using ROI-based optimization.

chapters.title: Unity Catalog
intro: Unity Catalog governs everything stored on the platform.
Access, policies, quality, cost, business definitions and sharing are set in one place.
Machine learning, agents and Genie all build on it.

points.title: Catalog and access
points.lead: Everything is now in one place. Access and lineage then have to be handled once for all of it.
bullets: **Unity Catalog** applies **one set of permissions**, lineage and audit to tables and files.
The catalog organizes every asset, and **Discover** lets users find them.
Lineage follows the data across the platform, and **external lineage** extends it to systems outside Databricks.
Access is granted **by role** or **by attribute**.
Users can **request access** to an asset.
Other engines access the same tables through **catalog commits** and the **Unity REST API**.
**Secrets** are stored and governed in the catalog.

points.title: Policy and classification
points.lead: Access policies depend on knowing what each table holds.
bullets: **Data classification** tags **sensitive data** such as PII.
**Governed tags** carry those labels, and **tag propagation** applies them to the data derived from a tagged table.
The tags feed **row- and column-level access policies**.
**Governance Hub** shows the state of governance in one dashboard.

points.title: Observability
points.effect: Get alerted when a table goes stale, and repair it as an audited job.
points.challenge: Data freshness is invisible and nobody is notified, so a stale table can go unnoticed. Repairing it is manual and risky.
points.pivot: **Data Quality Monitoring** now puts quality checks where access is controlled.
bullets: **Profiles** track metrics over time and detect **drift** in tables and in predictions.
Anomaly detection flags **stale or broken tables** and can trigger a repair job.
**Health indicators** show the quality and freshness of each table in the catalog.
Alerts go out by email, Slack or webhook.

pivot.text: Detects anomalies in data with automated remediation capabilities that are still emerging.

points.title: Cost and usage
bullets: **System tables** hold the platform's **billing and usage data**.
They are queried with SQL like any other table.
Audit logs and the history of automatic table maintenance are recorded there too.

points.title: Semantic definitions
points.lead: An answer is only trusted if "revenue" or "active customer" means the same thing as in the official reports.
bullets: **Metric views** define governed, reusable metrics in Unity Catalog, computed at query time.
**Domains** group assets by business domain.
**Pages** describe business concepts.

points.title: Data sharing
bullets: **OpenSharing** is the protocol for sharing data.
**SecureConnect** shares data that sits behind a firewall.
**Clean Rooms** let organizations work on shared data without exposing their raw data to each other.
**Marketplace** lists data, models and applications from other providers.

chapters.title: Data science and machine learning
intro: Data scientists work on the governed data in notebooks, with an AI assistant.
They build features, train on classic or serverless compute, track the work in MLflow, serve the models and automate their deployment.

points.title: Workspace
bullets: Data scientists work in notebooks that run Python, SQL, R and Scala directly on the **governed tables**.
Several people can edit the same notebook at once, and notebooks are **versioned in Git**.
Exploration uses the tools the team already knows: pandas, Spark, SQL and built-in data profiles.
**Genie Code** is the AI assistant inside notebooks, the SQL editor, pipelines and dashboards.
It **writes and explains code** from plain-language requests.
It works in a pane next to the notebook or on a **full page**.
A **command-line version**, in beta, brings it into the terminal and into CI pipelines.
It also runs **scheduled tasks**, including as a task in Lakeflow Jobs.

points.title: Feature engineering in Unity Catalog
points.effect: Build features once & reuse them across teams and models.
points.lead: Exploration ends in features, the inputs a model learns from. A feature computed one way for training and another way in production gives wrong predictions.
points.challenge: Teams duplicate the same features across projects. Nobody sees where each one comes from or who may use it.
points.pivot: **Feature Engineering in Unity Catalog** ends the duplication with one shared registry.
bullets: It keeps each definition in one place, with the same governance as the data.
Teams write features to **feature tables**, or declare them as **Feature Views**, which compute them automatically.
Stream Feature Views compute them from **streaming data**.
Training sets are built with **point-in-time correct joins**, and the same definitions feed predictions in production.
For real-time use, features are served from an **online store** on Lakebase.
**Feature serving** returns them over REST, and models look them up automatically at inference time.

challenge.text: Teams **duplicate** features across projects wasting resources
No visibility into feature **origins** and dependencies

pivot.text: **Shared** feature registry enables centralized reuse
Unity Catalog integration provides **access control** and compliance

points.title: Training compute
points.effect: Train at any scale, with GPUs on demand.
points.lead: Some datasets and models do not fit on one machine.
points.challenge: Distributed training code is hard to write correctly. GPUs are scarce. Clusters configured by hand are error-prone or sit idle.
points.pivot: **Databricks Runtime for Machine Learning** takes much of that work off the team.
bullets: It runs training on **classic clusters**, with managed libraries such as TorchDistributor, DeepSpeed and Ray.
AI Runtime provides **GPUs on demand** with no cluster to manage, and it scales to zero when the job ends.
The **AI Runtime SDK** spreads training across GPUs, and the **AI Runtime CLI** submits it from the command line.

features.name: Databricks Runtime for Machine Learning (classic compute)

effect.text: **Distributed** scaling across GPU workers handles any dataset size

challenge.text: Distributed training code is **complex** and difficult to write correctly
Manual **GPU** provisioning and cluster configuration is error-prone

pivot.text: **Managed** abstractions (DeepSpeed, TorchDistributor, Ray) hide distribution details
**Integrated** Databricks Runtime ML infrastructure handles resource allocation

points.title: MLflow 3 (ML lifecycle management)
points.effect: Repeat any experiment, and know which version runs in production.
points.lead: With features in place, the team trains many models and compares them. Comparing them requires that every result can be reproduced.
points.challenge: Each team keeps its metrics to itself. Nothing tracks model versions over time. Promotions are manual and error-prone.
points.pivot: **MLflow** handles the bookkeeping.
bullets: It records every training run with its parameters, metrics, code version and artifacts, so any result can be **reproduced and compared**.
Every model in production is registered in Unity Catalog with its versions, its aliases such as champion and challenger, and its **lineage** back to the training data.
Promoting a new version means **moving an alias**, and model update triggers or deployment jobs can start the next steps automatically.

effect.text: **Centralized** experiment tracking logs all parameters, metrics, and artifacts

challenge.text: Teams work in **isolation** with scattered metrics and results

pivot.text: Experiment tracking, autologging, and model management.
Model versioning, aliases, and lineage in Unity Catalog.

points.title: Model Serving (ML models)
points.effect: Put any model into production on serverless infrastructure.
points.lead: A registered version then has to serve traffic.
points.challenge: Each kind of model needs its own serving system, provisioned by hand, with access control split across them. Idle machines keep costing money.
points.pivot: **Model Serving** replaces them all as a single serverless service.
bullets: Its endpoints run the registered version, for real-time requests and for **batch scoring**.
**Custom model endpoints** serve models built with scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch or Hugging Face.
Endpoints scale with demand, **down to zero**.
They handle more than **25,000 queries per second** with low added latency.
Features are looked up from the online store **at serving time**.
**Endpoint telemetry** monitors the usage of each endpoint.
**Inference tables** log **every request and response**.

pivot.text: Model Serving provides serverless endpoints with pay-per-token, provisioned throughput, and batch billing.
**unified** control plane and REST API

points.title: Deployment automation
points.lead: Each change then has to reach production safely and the same way every time.
bullets: **Declarative Automation Bundles** describe code, jobs, models and their environments as **files in Git**.
The **Databricks CLI** deploys them from a terminal or a CI pipeline.
Each change goes from development to production through that **automated path**.

chapters.title: Agent development
intro: An agent combines models with company data and tools.
Teams choose the models, retrieve knowledge, connect tools, then build, deploy and give memory to the agent.
Business users build no-code agents with Genie Agents.

points.title: Model access
points.effect: Each task can get the best model, from any of the main providers.
points.challenge: Depending on one provider creates lock-in. Token spend grows unpredictably. Models from different providers are tested piece by piece.
points.pivot: **Foundation Model APIs** remove the dependency on any single vendor.
bullets: They give access through **one API** to models from providers that include Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta.
They are billed **per token**, with a **priority** option, or with **provisioned throughput**.
The catalog includes **OpenJev**, the Databricks judge model.
Because applications call the same API for every model, moving to a newer model stays a **small change**.
Models hosted at a provider are registered as **external models**, with their keys **stored centrally**.
**Unity Gateway** is the single access layer in front of all of these models.

effect.text: **Multi-provider** unified API (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Qwen, Grok, others)
**Unified endpoint** for A/B testing and model swapping

pivot.text: **Multi-provider** unified API (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Qwen, Grok, others)

points.title: Custom LLMs
points.effect: Adapt a model to your data with less GPU memory, paid by the minute.
points.lead: Sometimes a general model does not know the company's vocabulary or tasks well enough.
points.challenge: Full fine-tuning needs large amounts of GPU memory and is expensive and slow. Once tuned, the model often sits apart from the systems that serve the others.
points.pivot: **AI Runtime** now runs this work with lighter methods, and keeps the result on the platform.
bullets: It adapts an open model to company data with LoRA, QLoRA or full fine-tuning, on **serverless GPUs**.
The tuned model is logged in MLflow and served on **Model Serving** like any other model.

pivot.text: Fine-tuning runs on AI Runtime, with QLoRA, LoRA or full fine-tuning on serverless GPUs. Foundation Model Fine-tuning was removed on Aug 14, 2026.
**QLoRA/LoRA** parameter efficiency
integrate with **MLflow** and **Model Serving**

points.title: Batch inference: AI Functions
points.effect: Apply AI to large volumes of data and documents in place.
points.challenge: Running a model over company data usually means sending it to an outside service, building separate pipelines for documents and splitting the work into batches by hand. What comes back is unstructured.
points.pivot: **AI Functions** now run this work where the information already lives.
bullets: They call a model **from SQL** or from a pipeline to classify, extract or summarize data and documents at scale.
This needs no agent.
ai_query calls any model, ai_classify classifies, ai_extract extracts fields, ai_parse_document parses documents and ai_transcribe transcribes audio.
Classification and extraction also have a **no-code interface**.
The results come back with a **fixed schema**, and the data stays in Unity Catalog.
Applications call the same functions through a **REST API**.

challenge.text: model output is **unstructured** for downstream use

pivot.text: SQL- & pipeline-native AI for batch transformation of data and documents.

points.title: Knowledge retrieval
points.effect: Retrieve targeted data from documents, based on checked sources.
points.lead: An agent answers questions as they come. To answer well, it first has to find the right information.
points.challenge: Search indexes are built and kept in sync by hand. They often match on vectors alone.
points.pivot: **AI Search** fixes this by grounding answers in the right material.
bullets: ai_prep_search first splits the documents into chunks and prepares them for it.
AI Search indexes documents and tables for **vector, hybrid and full-text search**, keeps the index in sync with the Delta tables, and returns **citations**.
The **ai_search** function queries the index from SQL.
Agents can also use **Genie Agents** as a source of context.

features.name: AI Search (vector, hybrid and full-text search)
Genie Agents as a context source (see AI for business users)

effect.text: AI Search combines vector and keyword search with reranking, Delta sync, and citation tracking.

challenge.text: vector indices **slow to maintain** at scale

pivot.text: UC **lineage** and **citations** built-in
**hybrid** search (vector + BM25 + rerank)

points.title: Tools
points.effect: Agents reach tools through one governed route.
points.lead: Answering from documents only reads data. Many tasks also need actions, such as running a query, opening a ticket or changing code. Each of these tools needs a connection and permissions.
points.challenge: Teams write a custom connector for every one of them and host the servers themselves. Credentials pile up across agents. Tool use stays hidden.
points.pivot: The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** lets every connection be governed in one place instead.
bullets: It is the **standard way** for an agent to call tools.
Databricks runs **managed MCP servers** for its own services, such as Genie, AI Search and SQL.
Managed MCP connectors give **governed access** to Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack and GitHub.
Teams can register their own MCP servers or host them as Databricks Apps.
**Unity Catalog functions** and **skills** serve as tools as well.
Every tool is a **Unity Catalog object**, so permissions and audit work the same way as for data.
Databricks Sandbox runs the code an agent writes in an **isolated environment**, with scoped access to data.

pivot.text: Managed MCP servers provide governed agent access to Databricks services including analytics, search, and SQL.
MCP Services lets you register external MCPs as governed assets and deploy custom MCPs as Databricks Apps.

points.title: Agent build
points.effect: Build the agent you need, with any framework and any model.
points.lead: An agent combines retrieval and tools with its own logic.
points.challenge: Platforms often impose the framework and the model.
points.pivot: **Custom agents** lift these limits.
bullets: They are written in code with frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain or the OpenAI SDK.
They can use **any model** and any MCP tool.
**AI Bridge** packages connect these frameworks to Databricks: databricks-openai, databricks-langchain, databricks-dspy and databricks-mcp.
The **Agent Bricks CLI** creates a new project from templates.
Omnigent can also run them as a **meta-harness**.

pivot.text: **custom** agent logic and workflows
**choose** LangGraph, LangChain, OpenAI SDK
**choose** any model per use case

points.title: Agent deployment
points.lead: Once built, an agent has to run in production.
bullets: **AgentKit** is a **durable agent server**, shipped in the databricks-agentbricks SDK package.
Agents run on **Agent Runtime**, on Databricks Apps.
Applications query a deployed agent through the **Invocation API**, the **Responses API** or **SQL**.

points.title: Agent memory
points.effect: Agents remember what users told them.
points.challenge: Agents often start every conversation from nothing. Users then repeat their instructions each time.
points.pivot: **Managed memory** keeps that knowledge for them.
bullets: It is stored in **Lakebase**, and an agent searches it to **remember context** across conversations.
**Sessions** keep the state of each conversation.
Memory can also be built with **memory pipelines**.
Several agents can **share** the same memory.

pivot.text: **semantic search** retrieves past context
**long-term** Lakebase-backed storage

points.title: No-code agents: Genie Agents
bullets: Domain experts build agents **without code** in Genie Agents.
They are part of **AI for business users**.

chapters.title: Observability and evaluation
intro: Before an agent reaches users, its behavior has to be visible and its answers measured.
MLflow traces each request, evaluates the answers and versions the prompts.
Runtime telemetry covers what runs in production.

points.title: MLflow Tracing
points.effect: Trace request details and cost, step by step.
points.challenge: Agent chains are opaque to the people who run them. When an answer is wrong, the failing step is hard to isolate. The cost of each request is unknown.
points.pivot: **MLflow** makes every step visible.
bullets: It traces every request through the agent.
It records each model call, tool call and retrieval step, with inputs, outputs, **latency and tokens**, and it works with more than 30 agent frameworks.
When an answer is wrong, the trace shows **the step where it went wrong**.
The traces are stored in **Unity Catalog**.

pivot.text: MLflow provides end-to-end tracing for 30+ frameworks, LLM-based evaluation, and production monitoring.

points.title: MLflow evaluation
points.effect: Improve the quality of new agent versions.
points.lead: A trace shows one request. Judging quality needs a score across many requests.
points.challenge: Without such scores, traces are reviewed by hand and versions cannot be compared. Expert labels sit in separate spreadsheets.
points.pivot: **MLflow evaluation** measures the answers.
bullets: It applies **LLM judges** and custom **scorers** to traces.
It runs in batch before a release and continuously on **live traffic**.
Each agent version gets its own evaluation run, so versions can be compared.
The **Review App** lets domain experts test the agent in a chat interface and **label its answers**.
The labels attach to the traces and become **evaluation datasets**.
They are also used to align the judges with the experts.

pivot.text: **LLM judges** score each trace

points.title: Prompt Registry (prompt management)
points.effect: Know which prompt each version of an agent uses.
points.challenge: Prompts change with no record. Staging and production drift apart.
points.pivot: **Prompt Registry** keeps a version of every prompt.
bullets: Staging and production aliases point to them, so a change is tracked **like a code change**.
Each prompt is stored with its **model parameters**, such as the temperature.
Unity Catalog permissions control who can use each prompt.

pivot.text: version **history** per prompt

points.title: Runtime telemetry
points.lead: In production, each endpoint and each app also has to be watched.
bullets: Model Serving reports **telemetry** for each endpoint.
Databricks Apps export their **telemetry** to Unity Catalog, with agent traces in MLflow.
**Inference tables** store the requests and responses in Delta tables for quality analysis.
**System tables** record tokens, latency and errors for audit and troubleshooting.

chapters.title: AI governance and security
intro: Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway govern AI with the same rules as data.
The catalog holds the AI assets and their permissions.
The gateway applies policies, monitoring and cost controls to every call, including the calls of coding agents.

points.title: Unity Catalog for AI assets
points.effect: Each model, agent and tool can be traced to the data behind it and to everyone who used it.
points.challenge: Models, agents and tools are not governed as assets of their own. Permissions are enforced differently across them. External credentials are scattered. Nobody knows which data feeds which model.
points.pivot: **Unity Catalog** extends the existing rules to these assets.
bullets: It governs models, agents, tools and credentials in the **same way as tables and files**.
These assets include models, functions, hosted model services, external model provider services, memory stores, skills and traces.
Each of them is a Unity Catalog object with permissions, lineage and an audit trail.
Lineage follows the chain **from data to model to agent**.
Credentials for external services are stored in the catalog and **encrypted**.
Permissions also cover the use of **foundation models** and **AI Functions**, and **ABAC GRANT policies** apply to models and services.

features.name: ABAC GRANT policies for models and services

effect.text: **Audit logs** for all access, modification, and usage events

pivot.text: Unity Catalog for AI assets provides role-based access control, lineage tracking, and audit trails for models and agents.

points.title: Unity Gateway: policies
points.effect: Every model and tool call follows the same policies.
points.lead: The catalog sets who may use each asset. Each model call and each tool call also needs control at the moment it happens.
points.challenge: Prompts and responses go through without guardrails.
points.pivot: **Unity Gateway** puts one control plane in charge.
bullets: It sits in front of all model and tool traffic and is built on Unity Catalog.
**Service policies** set the rules for the calls to each service.
**LLM-as-a-judge policies** check prompts and responses with a model.
**Sensitive data** is redacted, and **partner guardrails** can be added.
**Request tags** attribute each call to a user, team or project.

pivot.text: **one control plane** fronts every provider

points.title: Unity Gateway: monitoring
points.effect: See who calls what, and keep a record of every call.
points.challenge: Teams connect to providers on their own, so nobody sees who uses which model. Nothing is logged for an audit.
points.pivot: **Unity Gateway** records the traffic that passes through it.
bullets: **Inference tables** log every request and response.
Usage is tracked **per user and team**, and a **usage dashboard** shows it.
A **unified trace table** collects the traces in one place.

challenge.text: **no central view** of who calls what

pivot.text: every request and response **logged**

points.title: Unity Gateway: cost and capacity
points.effect: Keep AI costs within budget.
points.challenge: Spend on models grows unchecked.
points.pivot: **Unity Gateway** puts limits on it, centrally.
bullets: **Budgets** and **cost caps** apply per user, team or project.
**Rate limits** cap the number of requests.
**Smart routing** picks the model for each request and falls back to another one when a provider is unavailable.

pivot.text: **budgets** cap spend centrally

points.title: Unity Gateway: coding agent governance
bullets: Coding agents connect to Unity Gateway with the **ug CLI**.
Their configuration is managed **centrally**.
Their model calls then follow the same policies, monitoring and cost controls as the rest of the AI traffic.

points.title: Security and compliance (Databricks AI Security Framework)
points.lead: Permissions and guardrails address known risks. A security team also needs the full list of risks and the control that covers each one.
bullets: The Databricks AI Security Framework lists the risks of AI systems and the controls that address them.
Version 3.0 covers 97 risks and 73 controls, including 35 risks **specific to agents**.
The controls include **least-privilege tool access** in Unity Catalog, sandboxed code execution, guardrails in Unity Gateway, and human review.
**Databricks Geos** keep data in a chosen geography, for **data residency**.
The **compliance security profile** turns on additional security controls for regulated workloads.

chapters.title: AI for business users
intro: Business users reach the governed data and the agents without writing code.
Genie One answers their questions in plain language, and Genie Agents carry the knowledge of each business area.
Genie also works inside the tools they already use, and applications run next to the data.

points.title: Genie One (conversational assistant)
points.effect: Anyone in the business can question the data directly.
points.challenge: Most people who need data do not write SQL. Their questions queue up at the data team. The answer often comes after the decision.
points.pivot: **Genie One** gives everyone a single entry point to the data.
bullets: It lets business users ask questions in **plain language**.
They get answers from governed company data, with citations and with **their own permissions** applied.
When a dashboard or an agent already answers the question, Genie One sends the user there.
It runs on the **web**, as a desktop app on macOS, and on **iOS** and **Android**.
Other AI assistants reach it through the **Genie One MCP server**.
**Web search** adds outside sources to its answers.
Users with **account-only access** can use it too.

effect.text: Users **answer** ad-hoc questions directly without SQL or waiting

challenge.text: Business users **blocked** by technical Databricks interface

pivot.text: Simplified, non-technical **front door** with natural language chat

points.title: Genie Agents (no-code agents)
points.effect: The knowledge of each business area becomes available to everyone in it.
points.lead: Once the definitions are shared, domain experts can package what they know for others.
points.challenge: Today that knowledge stays with a few people. Dashboards only answer the questions they were built for. Deeper analysis is spread across separate tools.
points.pivot: **Genie Agents** spread that expertise instead.
bullets: They let a domain expert build a **no-code assistant** for a business area.
The assistant can follow up on questions, run **multi-step analyses** and explain its reasoning, and it can be embedded in other applications.

effect.text: Domain experts **encode** logic once, shared as reusable agents

pivot.text: Domain experts **encode** logic once, shared as reusable agents

points.title: Genie Ontology (business context layer)
points.effect: Each metric has one certified definition, used everywhere.
points.lead: An answer is only trusted if "revenue" or "active customer" means the same thing as in the official reports.
points.challenge: Metrics are defined differently across dashboards, queries and teams. Business context is scattered in documents, chats and tickets. An AI can then pick an obsolete or draft definition.
points.pivot: **Genie Ontology** grounds answers in the certified version.
bullets: It holds those definitions.
Each KPI is **defined once**, as a metric view in Unity Catalog.
The ontology also learns **business context** from existing dashboards, queries and pipelines.
It ranks sources by certification, usage and freshness, so Genie answers from **certified definitions first**.

effect.text: Genie **uses** certified metrics and Pages in answering, with governance applied
Canonical **Unity Catalog Metric Views** define each KPI once, governed globally

challenge.text: Metrics defined **differently** across dashboards, queries, and teams
Business definitions **fragmented** across dashboards, SQL, docs, chat, tickets
Genie may **choose** obsolete or draft definitions over trusted sources

pivot.text: Learned business-context layer grounding Genie answers.

points.title: Genie integrations
points.lead: Many users spend their day in chat tools and spreadsheets.
bullets: Genie answers questions inside **Microsoft Teams** and **Slack**.
It also works in **Excel** and **Google Sheets**.
It is available in **Microsoft Copilot Cowork** as well.

points.title: AI/BI Dashboards
points.effect: Analysts and business people serve themselves, without waiting for a specialist.
points.challenge: Building a dashboard takes SQL skills, so requests wait.
points.pivot: **AI/BI Dashboards** come with an assistant.
bullets: A dashboard can be built from a **plain-language request**.
The assistant finds the tables, writes the queries and picks the charts, and the author **approves each step**.

effect.text: Analysts and business users **move** from question to governed dashboard independently

pivot.text: AI-assisted authoring, dashboard-level Genie, metric views.

points.title: Applications
points.effect: Data and AI applications run on the platform itself, next to the governed data.
points.lead: When the same question comes back every week, it is worth turning into a small application.
points.challenge: Usually each one runs on separate infrastructure, with its own identity management and secrets. It sits apart from the governed data. Access control and audit trails are hard to put in place.
points.pivot: **Databricks Apps** now hosts them itself.
bullets: Developers build applications with the **frameworks they already use**, such as Streamlit, Gradio, React or FastAPI, and deploy them.
**Databricks AppKit** is a framework for building them.
The apps run **serverless** on the platform.
They sign users in with the platform's identity and read data through Unity Catalog with **each user's permissions**.
Custom MCP servers run the same way.
App Spaces give admins **one place to govern** who deploys and uses which app.
**Genie App Builder** generates an app from a plain-language description, within the **limits the admins set**.

effect.text: **Serverless Databricks Apps** eliminate external hosting costs and complexity
Native **Unity Catalog integration** for permissions-aware data access

challenge.text: Apps require **separate infrastructure** outside Databricks platform
Apps require **separate identity management** and secrets handling
App-level access control and **audit trails** difficult to implement

pivot.text: Databricks Apps hosts interactive data and AI apps on Databricks, governed by Unity Catalog.

points.title: Genie ZeroOps (autonomous pipeline operations)
bullets: **Genie ZeroOps** runs **pipeline operations** on its own.
Its agent investigates a problem, proposes a fix in a sandbox, and waits for **human approval**.
It is announced.

points.title: Genie budgets (per-user limits)
bullets: **Genie budgets** set **per-user limits** on Genie usage.

chapters.title: Developer tools
intro: Developers bring their own coding agents to the platform and migrate existing SQL code.

points.title: Omnigent (coding agent harness)
points.effect: Coding agents share context and follow central policies.
points.challenge: Each coding-agent tool is its own isolated world, so content is copied between them by hand.
points.pivot: **Omnigent** puts them behind one interface.
bullets: It works with coding agents such as **Claude, Codex or Cursor**.
Agents are defined in **portable YAML**, for local or managed execution.
Developers can **share a live session**.
The managed version runs code in Databricks Sandbox.

pivot.text: **unified** interface across harnesses

points.title: Agentic code converter (SQL migration)
bullets: The **agentic code converter** converts SQL written for other systems into Databricks SQL.

chapters.title: Vertical applications
intro: Databricks builds complete applications for specific domains on the same platform.
Both are in private preview.

points.title: CustomerLake (customer data platform)
points.effect: Campaigns and personalization run on governed customer profiles that stay current.
points.challenge: Each system holds its own part of the customer, often duplicated and without lineage. Audiences are built and activated by hand.
points.pivot: **CustomerLake** now covers this work as a ready-made application.
bullets: In private preview, it builds **customer 360 profiles** on the lakehouse.
It joins transactions, behavior and engagement into one profile per customer.
AI-assisted **identity resolution** merges duplicate records.
Campaign agents create and **activate audiences**, and a real-time profile API feeds personalization.

effect.text: Embedded in lakehouse with **Unity Catalog** governance and audit
**Real-time profile API** with predictive models for instant attributes

pivot.text: CustomerLake delivers agentic capabilities for customer profiles, identity resolution, and campaign management.

points.title: Lakewatch (agentic SIEM)
points.effect: Keep every log and investigate faster.
points.lead: CustomerLake applies the platform to customer data. The same pattern applies to security data.
points.challenge: Telemetry is split across separate tools. Threat hunting and triage are manual. Detection rules are hard to version and test.
points.pivot: **Lakewatch** now lets agents share the load.
bullets: In private preview, it runs security operations on the lakehouse.
It keeps security, IT and business logs in one place at **object-storage cost**, so they no longer have to be deleted early.
Autonomous agents **investigate alerts** and help write detection rules, which are versioned and tested like code.

effect.text: **Unlimited** petabyte-scale ingestion and retention (object storage economics)
**Sub-second** queries across billions of records for rapid investigations
**Autonomous agents** for investigation, rule authoring, and data normalization

challenge.text: Security telemetry **siloed** in separate SIEM vendors
Detections **scattered** across tools; hard to version and test

pivot.text: Lakewatch provides agentic security information and event management with Panther integration.
